title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. $\hat\Pi_{0,3}$ is the profinite fundamental group of $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, i.e. the free profinite group $\hat F_2$. $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ is the profinite completion of the orientation-preserving 'extended' modular group. Grothendieck marks it as isomorphic to $\Pi'_{0,3}$. In modern terms it is $\widehat{PSL_2(\mathbb Z)} \simeq (\mathbb Z/2 * \mathbb Z/3)^\wedge$, which contains $\widehat{\Gamma(2)/\pm1} \simeq \hat F_2$ with quotient $PSL_2(\mathbb F_2)\simeq \mathfrak S_3$. This is the extension (31): $1\to\hat\Pi_{0,3}\to\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}\to\mathfrak S_3\to1$.

Goal. He wants to understand $\mathrm{Out}(\hat\Pi_{0,3})$ and $\mathrm{Out}(\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3})$ and how they relate through this extension. This continues the preceding pages on the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the conditions on pairs $(\lambda,f)$ for a Galois/GT-type action on $\hat F_2$.

Observation (32). Let $u$ be an automorphism of $G=\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ preserving $N=\hat\Pi_{0,3}$. It induces an automorphism of $\mathfrak S_3$, which is inner because $\mathrm{Out}(\mathfrak S_3)=1$. Composing $u$ with $\mathrm{int}$ of a lift gives $u_0$ in the same outer class that induces the identity on $\mathfrak S_3$. Now suppose $u_0$ and $\mathrm{int}(g)u_0$ both induce the identity on $\mathfrak S_3$. Then the image of $g$ in $\mathfrak S_3$ is central, hence trivial (the centre of $\mathfrak S_3$ is 1), so $g\in N$. Hence
$\{\text{outer automorphisms of } G \text{ preserving } N\} \simeq \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathfrak S_3\text{-id}}(G)/\mathrm{int}(N)$.

Next page. He goes on to show an automorphism of $G$ trivial on both $N$ and $\mathfrak S_3$ is trivial, using that $N$ has trivial centre and that the order-2 lifts generate $G$. He then asks which automorphisms of $\hat F_2$ extend; a necessary condition is that the induced outer automorphism commutes with the $\mathfrak S_3$-action. This is the germ of the 2- and 3-cycle relations defining $\widehat{GT}$.
errors: No real error on this page. The hypothesis 'induces a trivial outer automorphism on $\mathfrak S_3$' is automatically satisfied, since $\mathrm{Out}(\mathfrak S_3)=1$; the only real hypothesis is that $\hat\Pi_{0,3}$ is preserved. Grothendieck implicitly uses this.
Next page writes $SL(2,\mathbb Z)^\wedge$; the group with $\hat F_2$ as a normal subgroup of index 6 and quotient $\mathfrak S_3$ is $PSL(2,\mathbb Z)^\wedge$. This is a slip of notation.

ideas.what: Outer automorphisms of a group extension preserving the kernel, normalized to act trivially on the quotient: identification of the outer classes with $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{id\ on\ }\mathfrak S_3}(G)/\mathrm{Inn}(N)$, using that $\mathfrak S_3$ is complete (trivial centre, no outer automorphisms)
ideas.modern_name: Elementary group theory of extensions; the setting of $\mathrm{Out}(\hat F_2)$ versus $\mathrm{Out}(\widehat{PSL_2(\mathbb Z)})$ in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; the GT application is due to Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990–91), and Lochak–Schneps and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'Teichmüller tower' and $\mathrm{Out}$ of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ in general terms; this computation is not there as such

ideas.what: Viewing $\hat\Pi_{0,3}=\hat F_2$ as a normal subgroup of the profinite modular group with quotient $\mathfrak S_3$, so that extending automorphisms requires $\mathfrak S_3$-equivariance of the outer action
ideas.modern_name: The $\mathfrak S_3$-symmetry (2-cycle and 3-cycle) relations of $\widehat{GT}$; $\widehat{GT}$ acting on $\widehat{PSL_2(\mathbb Z)}$ and on $\hat\Gamma(2)$
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, the groups $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ and $\hat\pi_{1,1}$)

missed.claim: Shows Grothendieck, before Drinfeld/Ihara, explicitly setting up the comparison between outer automorphisms of $\hat F_2$ and of the profinite modular group via the $\mathfrak S_3$ extension. This is the structural root of the $\mathfrak S_3$-relations in $\widehat{GT}$. The page itself is routine, so it is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: Groupe des automorphismes ext. de $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ qui induisent dans $\mathfrak S_3$ un autom. ext. trivial ... $\simeq$ groupe des autom. de $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ qui induisent l'identité dans le quotient $\mathfrak S_3$, mod le sous-groupe des autom. int. par des $g\in\hat\Pi_{0,3}$
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents priority and motivation for the GT relations, as part of the 'équation des lacets' notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is an elementary group-theoretic normalization. Its interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck working toward the $\mathfrak S_3$-compatibility conditions later formalized in $\widehat{GT}$. Those conditions are well known now.
transcription_corrections: 'un autom. canonique[?] trivial' should read 'un autom. extérieur trivial' (manuscript: 'un autom. / extérieur trivial').
The struck-out word in the margin at the start of the paragraph is 'Proposition'; the text continues 'Notons que tt autom. ext. u de ...'. Here 'u' and 'u0' are names inserted above the line.
Under $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ in (31), the symbol '≀' with $\Pi'_{0,3}$ indicates an isomorphism $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}\simeq\hat\Pi'_{0,3}$.
Comment (not a transcription error): the passage 'son image dans $\mathfrak S_3$ soit central, i.e. $=1$' is correctly transcribed.
